description: Start indoors 6–8 weeks before last frost. Transplant deep — buried stems grow extra roots. Cage or stake early; mulch once soil warms.
name: Tomato

description: Needs warm soil (75–85°F) to germinate — a heat mat helps a lot. Transplant only after nights stay above 55°F.
name: Pepper (Bell)

description: Super-hots can take 3+ weeks to sprout — be patient. Slight stress (less water) once fruiting boosts heat.
name: Pepper (Hot)

description: Direct-sow after frost; hates transplanting. Trellis to save space and keep fruit straight. Pick often — big cukes slow the vine.
name: Cucumber

description: One plant feeds a neighborhood. Harvest at 6–8 inches; oversized fruit signals the plant to quit.
name: Zucchini

description: Give vines room to roam. Cure harvested fruit in sun 1–2 weeks for thicker skin and sweeter flesh.
name: Winter Squash

description: Pinch flower buds relentlessly — flowering turns leaves bitter. Harvest from the top to force bushy growth.
name: Basil

description: Cool-season crop; bolts in heat. Sow every 2 weeks for continuous harvest. Shade cloth extends the season.
name: Lettuce

description: Sow as soon as soil can be worked in spring, again in late summer for fall. Bolts fast once days lengthen.
name: Spinach

description: Sweetens after frost. Harvest outer leaves; the center keeps producing. Watch for cabbage worms.
name: Kale

description: Keep the seedbed evenly moist until sprouts show — a board over the row helps. Thin ruthlessly or roots fork.
name: Carrot

description: Fastest payoff in the garden. Sow with slow carrots to mark the row. Gets pithy if left too long.
name: Radish

description: Each 'seed' is a cluster — thin to one. Greens are edible too. Steady water prevents woody roots.
name: Beet

description: Direct-sow after frost; seeds rot in cold wet soil. Pick every couple days to keep pods coming.
name: Bean (Bush)

description: Needs a sturdy trellis before sowing. Produces longer than bush types from the same footprint.
name: Bean (Pole)

description: Sow 4–6 weeks before last frost. Fades in summer heat — plan a fall round too.
name: Pea

description: Plant sets pointy-end-up as soon as soil is workable. Stop watering when tops fall over; cure before storing.
name: Onion (from sets)

description: Plant cloves in late October, mulch heavily, harvest early summer when lower leaves brown. Hardneck suits cold zones.
name: Garlic

description: Plant certified seed potatoes, eyes up. Hill soil over stems as they grow — light turns tubers green and bitter.
name: Potato

description: Grown from slips, not seeds — plant after soil is warm. Needs a long season; black plastic mulch helps up north.
name: Sweet Potato

description: Plant in blocks, not single rows, for pollination. Heavy feeder — side-dress when knee-high.
name: Corn

description: Loves heat — transplant late, mulch with black plastic. Flea beetles love seedlings; row cover early.
name: Eggplant

description: Soak seeds overnight to speed sprouting. Pick pods at 3–4 inches daily — they go woody fast.
name: Okra

description: Bolts at the first hint of heat. Succession-sow every 2–3 weeks; let one plant go to seed for coriander.
name: Cilantro

description: Direct-sow where it will live — taproot hates moving. Self-sows freely; great for beneficial insects.
name: Dill

description: Slow to sprout — pour hot (not boiling) water over the row to hurry it. Biennial; overwinters in mild zones.
name: Parsley

description: Perennial — plant once, snip for years. Divide clumps every 3–4 years. Pretty purple flowers are edible.
name: Chives

description: Perennial that demands sharp drainage — sandy soil or a pot. Shear after flowering to keep it compact.
name: Thyme

description: Perennial; flavor peaks just before flowers open. Spreads — give it its own corner or a container.
name: Oregano

description: Slow from seed — a nursery start saves a season. Overwinters outdoors only in mild zones; otherwise pot it and bring in.
name: Rosemary
